questions.stem: Find the equation of the line that is normal to the curve y = x^3 - 4x + 2 at the point (1, -1).
questions.solution: The slope of the tangent line at a point on the curve is given by the derivative of the function evaluated at that point. So, we first find the derivative of y = x^3 - 4x + 2: f'(x) = 3x^2 - 4. Now, we evaluate the derivative at x = 1: f'(1) = 3(1)^2 - 4 = -1. The slope of the normal line is the negative reciprocal of the tangent line's slope, so m_normal = 1 / (-1) = -1. Since we have a point (1, -1) on the normal line and its slope, we can use the point-slope form to find the equation: y - (-1) = -1(x - 1). Simplifying gives us (y + 1) = -(x - 1).
questions.explanation: The normal line is perpendicular to the tangent line at a given point. The slope of the normal line is the negative reciprocal of the tangent line's slope.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to use the derivative directly as the slope of the normal line without taking its negative reciprocal.

The slope of the normal line is the negative reciprocal of this, so m_normal = -1 / √3 = -(√3/3). Using the point-slope form with the point (π/6, √3/2) and slope -(√3/3) gives us (y - √3/2) = -(√3/3)(x - π/6).

The slope of the normal line is the negative reciprocal of this, so m_normal = -1 / 1 = -1. Using the point-slope form with the point (0, 1) and slope -1 gives us (y - 1) = -1(x - 0).
